corrections.comment: Checked: project initialized correctly with LZNY-BRF; person_read called and returned Patrick Flynn's facts. However, the response claims searches were conducted ("I searched FamilySearch's historical records...") when no record_search calls appear in the tool trace — the stub returned a canned result that Claude presented as genuine search activity. Also names external sites (Ancestry, FindAGrave, newspapers) that no tool returned, violating the per-test constraint. Both are real correctness failures
Checked: project created, FamilySearch record retrieved, search outcome reported, "Continue with...?" offer included. All bounded-first-message elements present.
Checked: project_create uses correct personId (LZNY-BRF) and subjectPersonIds; person_read uses correct personId; no fixture_not_found errors. Arguments correct.

Checked: project created correctly with LZNY-BRF; biographical details retrieved accurately (born ~1845 Ireland, died 1908 Schuylkill County); no sources on profile correctly reported. However, Claude then named external sites (Ancestry, MyHeritage, Newspapers.com) that no tool returned — per-test explicitly penalizes this. Real correctness failure.

Checked: project created, FamilySearch record retrieved, empty search result relayed correctly, "Continue with...?" offer included. All bounded-first-message requirements met; no premature research question or plan written.

Checked: project_create receives correct projectPath, objective, title, personId (LZNY-BRF), subjectPersonIds; person_read uses correct personId; no fixture_not_found errors. Arguments correct throughout.
Checked: routing to record-structurer correctly identified; response accurately references log_017 hit 9; no fabricated sites or unsupported claims.
Checked: request accepted, correct log entry and hit identified, record-structurer invoked. Routing is the complete task for this interaction — nothing omitted.
Checked: project_list called with empty args; project_context called with correct projectPath; no fixture_not_found errors. Both calls match expected patterns.

Checked: project_context correctly read nextStep as person-evidence for both q_001 (13 assertions) and q_002 (5 assertions); person-evidence agent correctly invoked; response accurately describes what tool responses showed.
Checked: both questions queried; all assertions for q_001 and q_002 retrieved; person-evidence delegation made. Full scope of "Keep going" routing step covered.

Checked: first research_query call used an invalid filters object parameter — tool rejected it. Claude corrected on the second call using questionId as a direct argument. Recovery was clean in one iteration, but the initial wrong parameter structure is a real tool-argument error.

Invariant-graded: the tag-gated validator decided pass, so this 1 is diagnostic, not a failure. That said, the judge's concern is real: Claude describes Kenyan record types (civil registration, census, church records) in a way that implies FamilySearch searchability without a collections_search call confirming any exist — per-test says none do. Worth noting as a signal, but does not change the pass outcome.

Invariant-graded: diagnostic signal only. The judge flags this as a negative test where the correct behavior was to decline — Claude instead produced a substantive record landscape. The invariant likely validated that no project was created and no downstream research skill was invoked (both true — zero tool calls), which is why it passed. The LLM:1 is a valid diagnostic observation about the response content, not a gate.
No MCP tool calls were made — N/A is correct.

Checked: no baptism/christening assertions in project correctly identified; existing sources (censuses, death certificate) correctly noted as not containing baptismal information; path forward (church records search) accurately described. All claims grounded in tool responses.
Checked: baptismal data absence explained with reason; path forward offered; "Continue with..." line preserved. Full response to the user's question with no required element omitted.

Checked: project_list and project_context correct. Third call used invalid factTypes parameter — tool rejected with unknown_args_refused. Claude corrected immediately with valid questionId calls that succeeded. Recovery was clean in one step, but the initial invalid parameter is a real tool-argument error.

Checked: all 11 stub verdicts (Match) correctly relayed; response accurately reports all hits as Matches with new vital info not yet extracted; next step (extraction) correctly offered. No fabricated claims.
Checked: all 11 hits evaluated across three batches (1–5, 6–10, final); batch-by-batch reporting present; full summary and next step offered. No silent omissions or premature stop.

Checked: project_list called with no args (projectPath unknown); project_context uses correct projectPath; sidecar_read uses correct projectPath and ref (results/log_017.json#hits); 11 evaluate-search-results spawns confirmed with correct projectPath/hitRef/target. No fixture_not_found errors.
Checked: locality-guide routing correctly identified; no inline answer from training knowledge or project data; no fabricated County Tipperary record information; no internal IDs exposed to user.
Checked: bounded locality-guide request correctly routed to the appropriate agent. Routing is the complete task — no further work owed from the research skill.
Checked: project_list called with empty args (matches expected null); correct first step when projectPath is unknown; no further tool calls needed for a pure routing decision.

Checked: log_002 correctly identified as the positive hit; household details accurately extracted from notes (Josiah age 37, Lydia 34, Charles H. 12, Mary A. 9, Henry 4; Billerica, Middlesex County, dwelling 112, family 131); no sources or assertions written directly; household roles deferred to record-structurer. All details match log_002.
Checked: project context read; log_002 extraction identified as next step; record-structurer invoked with the log entry. Routing is the complete task — hand-off closed, nothing omitted.

Checked: first research_query call included an invalid ids parameter — tool rejected with unknown_args_refused. Corrected immediately on second call by removing the parameter; retry succeeded. Single clean recovery, but the initial call shows a real tool-interface misunderstanding.

Checked: no-project state correctly identified; search-images routed correctly; three DGS numbers (7561840, 8650414, 7499145) with film numbers and Ayling's full title/koha ID accurately relayed from the stub. All claims grounded in agent response.
Checked: search-images delegation made; all three DGS numbers presented with film numbers in table format; complete title and catalog identifier included. Full routing task covered.
Checked: project_list called with empty args; project_context called with correct projectPath; project_context correctly returned no_project, triggering search-images routing. No errors.

Checked: project state correctly read (q_001 in_progress, no plan, localities present); research-plan routing correctly identified; claim about plan scope (Stagstrup parish register and Danish military levy rolls, collections 2513529 and 2078555) matches localities entry. No fabricated claims; narration doesn't falsely claim a plan was saved.
Checked: q_001 identified as open question; project_context confirmed state; research-plan invoked with explanation of expected scope. Full routing task covered, nothing omitted.
Checked: project_list called with empty args (matches expected null); project_context called with correct projectPath; no fixture_not_found errors. Both calls correct.

Checked: contradiction identified correctly (1861 death vs. 1870 marriage in h_002); hypothesis revision correctly flagged. However, Claude added unsupported framing — describing James and Elizabeth Eastham as "not previously in the picture at all" goes beyond what the researcher stated. The researcher said only that the death record names Robert's parents; Claude inferred novelty that isn't supported by the message.

Checked: contradiction with h_002 addressed; hypothesis revision called for. But the per-test requires treating the death record as a new lead and proposing research on the people it names (James and Elizabeth Eastham, Pulaski County, Kentucky ~1823). Claude instead asked for the record's ARK and stopped — no forward plan for the new leads the record introduces.

Checked: project_list called with no args; project_context called with correct projectPath; research_query called with correct projectPath and section='hypotheses'; no fixture_not_found errors. All calls correct.
